capabilities: Import .eml/.msg emails by dragging them in or watching a drop folder
Sort emails into keyword, sender, and domain filter categories with child categories
Track task status and milestones from phrases found in emails
Visualize activity, senders, and task status with dashboard charts
Encrypt stored records with a passphrase and recovery key
disambiguation: Not an email client; it stores only short reference records of imported emails and never saves bodies, recipients, or attachments.
extras: Desktop-only (uses Node file system access). Uninstalling the plugin deletes records.json, so export to CSV first. Records live in the plugin folder and will sync if a sync tool includes plugin folders. Works fully offline with no network access or telemetry.
problem: Obsidian has no way to import emails and turn correspondence into categorized, status-tracked records without storing email content in the vault.

relations.evidence: Classic Outlook (Windows): drag a message onto the dashboard drop zone, or anywhere in Obsidian.
Gmail (web): open the email → ⋮ → Download message → drop the .eml file.

summary: Email tracker that imports .eml/.msg files, sorts them into filter-based categories, and tracks task status and activity on a dashboard.
